description: AST-tester probes for Kotlin — exercises grammar (suspend, trailing lambdas, sealed interfaces, extension funcs, inline+crossinline), chunker, and ranker on idiomatic Kotlin coroutines patterns.

probes.query: how does a coroutine job get cancelled and propagate cancellation to its children
probes.notes: NL behavior probe. JobSupport is the open class that implements the full job state machine (cancelImpl, makeCancelling, childCancelled). It is 1582 lines with deeply nested private inner classes (InvokeOnCancelling, ChildHandleNode, etc.) — a stress test for parsers that mishandle open classes with many nested/anonymous objects and private inline helper lambdas inside member functions.

probes.query: how does withContext switch coroutine dispatcher while preserving structured concurrency
probes.notes: NL behavior probe. withContext is a suspend fun declared as `public suspend fun <T> withContext(context: CoroutineContext, block: suspend CoroutineScope.() -> T)`. The trailing lambda is typed as `suspend CoroutineScope.() -> T` — a higher-kinded function type receiver — which parsers that only handle simple block arguments often mis-chunk, splitting the KDoc from the declaration.

probes.query: how does runBlocking block the current thread until all coroutines inside complete
probes.notes: NL behavior probe. runBlocking is the JVM-specific entry point (`public fun <T> runBlocking(context, block: suspend CoroutineScope.() -> T): T`). It is the canonical trailing-lambda coroutine builder for tests and main functions, living in a platform-specific source set (jvm/src), which exercises the indexer's handling of multi-platform Kotlin source trees.

probes.query: launch coroutine builder extension function on CoroutineScope
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe. `launch` is declared as `public fun CoroutineScope.launch(...)` — an extension function with a trailing lambda parameter `block: suspend CoroutineScope.() -> Unit`. The ergonomic call site is `scope.launch { ... }` or `launch { ... }` inside a CoroutineScope. This is the single most common trailing-lambda pattern in Kotlin and a canonical parser stress test: `launch { body }` looks like a function call statement with a block, which tree-sitter grammars that lack a `trailing_lambda` node can misparse as a property access.

probes.query: cancelAndJoin suspend extension function that cancels a Job and waits for it to finish
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe. `cancelAndJoin` is declared as `public suspend fun Job.cancelAndJoin()` — a top-level suspend extension function. This pattern (top-level suspend extension on an interface) is commonly chunked incorrectly: parsers that anchor on class/object bodies may emit it as a free-floating chunk without its receiver type, losing the `Job.` qualifier from the indexed symbol.

probes.query: suspendCancellableCoroutine inline function for integrating callback APIs with coroutines
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe. `suspendCancellableCoroutine` is declared as `public suspend inline fun <T> suspendCancellableCoroutine(crossinline block: (CancellableContinuation<T>) -> Unit): T`. The combination of `suspend`, `inline`, and `crossinline` on a type-parameterized function is a grammar edge case: tree-sitter Kotlin grammars must correctly parse the modifier order, and chunkers must not split the `contract { }` block that immediately follows from the enclosing function body.

probes.query: produce coroutine builder with trailing lambda that sends values into a channel
probes.notes: Grammar edge-case probe — TRAILING LAMBDA. `produce` is declared as `public fun <E> CoroutineScope.produce(...)` with a trailing `block: suspend ProducerScope<E>.() -> Unit`. Its idiomatic call site is `produce { send(value) }`. The ProducerScope receiver on the lambda is a second-order extension type that causes naive Kotlin parsers to misparse the block as a lambda literal rather than a function body, dropping the chunk boundary between the `produce` declaration and its `ProducerScope` implementation class above it in the same file.

probes.query: sealed interface SelectClause hierarchy used in select expression DSL
probes.notes: Grammar edge-case probe — SEALED HIERARCHY. Select.kt defines a sealed interface hierarchy: `SelectClause` (root), `SelectClause0`, `SelectClause1<out Q>`, `SelectClause2<in P, out Q>`, `SelectBuilder<in R>`, and `SelectInstance<in R>` — all sealed interfaces with variance annotations. This is the most complex sealed hierarchy in the repo and exercises parsers on: (a) sealed interfaces (not sealed classes), (b) use-site variance in type parameters (`in`, `out`), and (c) multiple sealed declarations in one file, which can cause chunker boundary errors if the parser uses class-body nesting depth to decide chunk splits.
